newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares power toward records, eye U.S..
newsitem.headline: German shares power toward records, eye U.S..

text.p: Relief at the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates powered German shares close to all-time highs in afternoon trade on Wednesday.
"If everything looked negative yesterday, it all looks positive now," said a Frankfurt trader.
The IBIS DAX index was up 91.45 points, or 2.6 percent, at 3,607.65 points at 1243 GMT, and looked set to hold those gains barring a sharp fall on Wall Street, dealers said.
"We've had the good news and now we want to see Wall Street confirm that reading," said another dealer.
"But the mood here is very optimistic."
June DTB DAX futures were up 82.5 at 3,608.5 points.

The gains, initially driven by traders wrong-footed by the decision to leave U.S. rates unchanged, had been consolidated by keen buying interest, albeit focused on stocks at the centre of the news, dealers said.
Metals and chemicals firm Degussa AG remained among the favourites after utility Veba AG announced plans to buy a large stake in it at well above market value.
Degussa was trading up 9.31 percent, or 7.10 marks, at 83.40 marks, below the Veba buy price of 86.80 marks.
Veba was trading up 1.19 marks at 99.71 marks.

The deal, which is expected to lead to strategic link-ups between Veba's Huels unit and Degussa, was viewed as positive for both companies, especially as Veba said it will not have to raise capital to finance the deal.
Thomas Deser of BHF Bank raised Veba to a buy from hold and raised its EPS forecast by 10 pfennigs over each of the next two years to 5.70 marks in 1997 and 6.30 marks in 1998.
Earnings advantages for Degussa were seen as longer term.
Bank shares also rallied, with the DAX-100 bank shares index clocking up gains of 2.6 percent.

Dealers linked their gains partly with the Veba-Degussa deal, since Dresdner Bank AG was among three companies who sold Degussa stock and stands to gain 789 million marks from the deal. Dresdner was up 1.60 marks at 62.25 marks.
Dealers said news of the acquisition may have boosted hopes that German banks were poised to offload more of their substantial portfolios of industrial shareholdings.
